subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Know the purpose of a brochure.
Find the features of a good brochure.
Plan and write a brochure with strong adjectives.

tf.s: The model brochure wants people to come water skiing at Qantab Beach.
A good brochure often starts with questions to the reader.

tf.why: Short paragraphs are easier to read.

tf.s: Brochures talk to the reader using 'you' and 'we'.
tf.why: Right, 'you' and 'we' make it friendly and direct.
Well done, they are strong, exciting adjectives.

tf.s: The last sentence of a brochure does not matter.
tf.why: An interesting final sentence helps readers remember.

tf.s: 'The food was terrible' uses a stronger adjective than 'The food was very bad'.
tf.why: Yes, terrible is a strong adjective.

tf.s: A brochure should be boring so people trust it.
tf.why: A brochure should be exciting to persuade readers.

tf.s: You can use a checklist to check your brochure.
tf.why: A checklist helps you include every feature.

tf.s: 'The view was very nice' is the strongest way to describe a great view.
tf.why: Stronger words are stunning or amazing.

boxes.q: What is the model brochure about?
boxes.why: It invites people to water ski at Qantab Beach.

boxes.q: How does the model brochure start?
boxes.why: It starts with questions to make readers interested.
'You' and 'we' speak directly to the reader.
Short paragraphs are easy for readers.

boxes.q: Rewrite strongly: The weather was very bad.
boxes.why: Awful is a strong word for very bad.

boxes.q: Rewrite strongly: The view was very nice.
boxes.why: Stunning is a strong word for very nice.

boxes.q: Which is a good brochure title?
boxes.why: A good title is short and exciting.

boxes.q: Which is a good final sentence?
o: Book today for the adventure of your life!
boxes.why: An exciting ending makes readers want to act.

boxes.q: Which word is an exciting adjective?
What do you do after writing your brochure?
boxes.why: Checking helps you improve your work.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of the model brochure?
o: to get people to come water skiing at Qantab Beach
to tell a story about a trip
mcq.why: The brochure persuades people to try water skiing.

mcq.q: Which is a feature of a good brochure?
mcq.why: A good brochure ends with an interesting sentence.

mcq.q: Why does a brochure start with questions?
Which two adjectives are in the model brochure?
mcq.why: The brochure uses exciting adjectives like brilliant and gorgeous.

mcq.q: Rewrite with a strong adjective: The food was very bad.
o: The food was very very bad.
mcq.why: Terrible is a strong adjective for very bad.

mcq.q: Choose the best opening question for a paragliding brochure.
o: Have you ever wanted to fly like a bird?
mcq.why: A good question makes readers dream about the activity.

mcq.q: Which sentence speaks directly to the reader?
o: You will love our gorgeous beach!
mcq.why: Using 'you' talks directly to the reader.

mcq.q: Which brochure plan is the best?
o: exciting title, questions, strong adjectives, short paragraphs, interesting ending
mcq.why: It has all the features from the How to write box.

mcq.q: Why is 'The view was stunning' better than 'The view was very nice' in a brochure?
o: A strong adjective is more persuasive.
mcq.why: Strong adjectives make readers want to come.

mcq.q: A student's brochure has no questions and no 'you'. What should the student add?
mcq.why: Questions and 'you' make the brochure speak to the reader.
